subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Connecting two cells in series rather than one cell will generally:
questions.explain: Cells connected in series add their voltages together, increasing the total supply voltage to the circuit.

questions.q: Programming a product's behaviour with a microcontroller rather than fixed wiring is an advantage because:
options: It removes the need for any input devices
It increases the size of the product
The behaviour can be changed by editing the program without rewiring
questions.explain: A programmable microcontroller lets designers change a product's function by altering software, avoiding costly hardware changes.

questions.q: The unit used to measure electrical resistance is the:
questions.explain: Resistance is measured in ohms; voltage is measured in volts and current in amperes.

questions.q: In a flowchart used to program a microcontroller, a diamond shape usually represents:
questions.explain: In flowcharts, the diamond is a decision box that tests a condition and branches the program along yes or no paths.

questions.q: A piezo or PIR sensor that detects movement would be classed in a system as:
questions.explain: A movement sensor detects a change and feeds a signal into the system, so it is an input device.

questions.q: As light falling on an LDR increases, its resistance:
questions.explain: An LDR's resistance falls as light intensity rises, allowing more current to flow in bright conditions.

questions.q: A transistor in a circuit is most commonly used as:
questions.explain: A transistor can act as an electronic switch, turning an output on or off, or as an amplifier in a circuit.

questions.q: A diode is a component that allows current to flow:
questions.explain: A diode permits current to flow in one direction only, blocking it in the reverse direction.

questions.q: One key reason electronic systems are built into modern products is that they:
options: Always make products cheaper to throw away
Allow products to sense, respond and be controlled automatically
Remove the need for any materials
questions.explain: Electronics let products sense their surroundings and respond automatically, adding functions like automatic lighting or temperature control.

questions.q: A simple push-to-make switch acts as which part of a system?
questions.explain: A switch is an input device that the user operates to send a signal into the system.

questions.q: In circuit diagrams, two parallel lines of unequal length (one longer, one shorter) usually represent:
questions.explain: The standard symbol for a cell is a long line (positive) and a shorter thicker line (negative); batteries combine several cells.

questions.q: A microcontroller is used in products because it:
options: Only ever works as a battery
Can be programmed to control inputs and outputs flexibly
questions.explain: A microcontroller is a programmable chip that can read inputs and control outputs, allowing one component to perform many control tasks.

questions.q: An LDR (light-dependent resistor) is which type of component in a system?
questions.explain: An LDR is an input sensor whose resistance changes with light level, supplying information to the process stage.

questions.q: A motor in an electronic product is best classified as:
options: An output device that converts electrical energy into motion
An input device that senses movement
A process device that makes decisions
questions.explain: A motor is an output device, turning electrical energy into rotary mechanical motion.

questions.q: When connecting an LED in a circuit, a resistor is usually placed in series to:
options: Make the LED brighter than its maximum
Limit the current so the LED is not damaged
questions.explain: A series current-limiting resistor protects the LED by keeping the current within its safe operating limit.

questions.q: A potential divider made from two resistors is used to:
options: Increase the supply voltage above the battery
Provide a fixed lower output voltage from a higher supply
questions.explain: A potential divider uses two resistors to split a supply voltage, providing a smaller, fixed output voltage.

questions.q: The main purpose of a capacitor in a basic circuit is to:
questions.explain: A capacitor stores electrical charge and can be used for timing, smoothing and energy-storage functions in circuits.

questions.q: A relay is useful in a circuit because it allows:
options: A small control current to switch a larger separate circuit
Charge to be stored long term
questions.explain: A relay is an electromagnetic switch letting a small current control a much larger or separate circuit safely.

questions.q: An Arduino is best described as:
options: A programmable microcontroller board for controlling inputs and outputs
questions.explain: An Arduino is a programmable microcontroller board used to read sensors and control outputs in projects.

questions.q: Which of these is an output device?
questions.explain: A buzzer is an output device that converts an electrical signal into sound; switches, LDRs and thermistors are inputs.

questions.q: The systems approach to electronics describes the order of blocks as:
questions.explain: A system is modelled as input leading to process leading to output, where a signal is received, acted upon, and then produces an action.

questions.q: A thermistor is a sensor that responds to changes in:
questions.explain: A thermistor changes its resistance with temperature, making it an input device for temperature-sensing circuits.

specSource: AQA GCSE Design and Technology (8552) specification; Electronic Systems
